title: Animals And Birds Arabic Summary For The 7th Degree Of The 1st Station

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the three truths together show about all kinds of animals?
questions.answer: They show that all animal species together testify to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How is the whole earth pictured after this shared testimony of animals is described?
questions.answer: It is pictured like a huge living being declaring belief in Allah in a way fitting its greatness.

questions.question: Who receives this testimony from the earth in the passage’s image?
questions.answer: The inhabitants of the heavens receive it.

questions.question: What was the traveller’s response to this scene?
questions.answer: He recognized its meaning clearly and fully understood it.

questions.question: In this section, how do animals and birds give their testimony?
questions.answer: They do so through their senses, abilities, limbs, and bodily parts, all working in an ordered and meaningful way.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by calling these features “words”?
questions.answer: It suggests that their very design and function communicate praise and evidence of their Creator.

questions.question: Which three major divine qualities are connected to the making of animals in this passage?
questions.answer: Will, purpose, and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about bringing living things into existence?
questions.answer: It presents creation as something done intentionally, not randomly or without knowledge.

questions.question: How does distinction and decoration among animals support the main claim?
questions.answer: Their differences and beauty show deliberate choice and careful design, pointing to one wise Creator.

questions.question: What is meant by proportioning and forming according to wisdom?
questions.answer: It means animals are given fitting shapes and balanced forms with wise order behind them.

questions.question: From what simple beginnings do these many animal forms appear?
questions.answer: They appear from eggs and reproductive drops that are alike or very similar.

questions.question: Why is the contrast between similar beginnings and countless forms important?
questions.answer: It shows that such variety cannot come from the starting materials alone, but points to divine power and knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number of starting materials compared with the number of forms?
questions.answer: The beginnings are limited, but the resulting forms are countless and highly varied.

questions.question: What central belief is affirmed at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: That only Allah is truly worthy of worship and that His existence and unity are clearly indicated by creation.

questions.question: What is the main message of the passage about animals and birds?
questions.answer: Their shared existence and design serve as a united witness to Allah’s existence and oneness.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak of a “consensus” among animals?
questions.answer: Because all of them, in their own created way, point to the same truth rather than giving mixed messages.

questions.question: What comparison is used to help the reader imagine the earth’s testimony?
questions.answer: The earth is compared to a giant person speaking a declaration of faith.

questions.question: What does this comparison add to the meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It makes the testimony feel broad, alive, and impossible to ignore.

questions.question: In what two broad ways do animals and birds praise and testify?
questions.answer: Through their inner capacities and senses, and through their outer body parts and physical systems.

questions.question: What do the balanced and orderly qualities of these features imply?
questions.answer: They imply planning, control, and skill in their creation.

questions.question: Which part of the passage points to deliberate choice rather than accident?
questions.answer: The part linking creation to will and giving each creature distinct features and decoration.

questions.question: How does the passage connect beauty in animals with faith?
questions.answer: Their beauty is treated as a sign of intentional design, not as something meaningless.

questions.question: What role does purpose play in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Purpose shows that creatures were made for meaningful ends, which points to a knowing Maker.

questions.question: Why is wisdom mentioned along with shaping and measuring?
questions.answer: Because their forms are not only made, but made in fitting and well-judged ways.

questions.question: What surprising fact about animal origins is highlighted?
questions.answer: Vast numbers of different creatures come from beginnings that look alike or nearly alike.

questions.question: How does this fact strengthen the argument for divine unity?
questions.answer: It shows one Creator can produce endless variety from simple sources by His power and wisdom.

questions.question: What can a reader infer from the passage’s stress on order, variety, and limit?
questions.answer: That creation is controlled and meaningful, not self-made or chaotic.

questions.question: If you stated the passage’s conclusion in one sentence, what would it be?
questions.answer: The created nature of animals and birds clearly points to Allah alone as the necessary and one Creator.

questions.question: What do the three truths lead all animal species to declare together?
questions.answer: They lead them to bear witness that there is no deity except Allah.

questions.question: Why is the image of the earth speaking powerful in this section?
questions.answer: It gathers the testimony of countless creatures into one grand, unified witness.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the body of an animal?
questions.answer: Its parts and systems are meaningful signs that show careful creation.

questions.question: Why are senses and powers included in the testimony, not just visible limbs?
questions.answer: Because both inner abilities and outer organs show design and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by linking creation with will?
questions.answer: It means living beings are brought into existence by conscious divine choice.

questions.question: What does linking distinction and adornment with purpose add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that animals are not only different and beautiful, but made that way for meaningful reasons.

questions.question: What does linking form and measure with wisdom emphasize?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that their structure is suitable, balanced, and intelligently arranged.

questions.question: How does the passage move from observation to belief?
questions.answer: It starts with what is seen in animals and then reasons from those signs to Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: Why are eggs and reproductive drops mentioned?
questions.answer: They show that many different creatures come from simple, similar, and limited starting points.

questions.question: What is the significance of animals having countless forms?
questions.answer: It points to a Creator whose knowledge and power are far beyond the materials themselves.

questions.question: What does the word “definite” suggest about the strength of the evidence?
questions.answer: It suggests the indication is firm, clear, and not weak or doubtful.

questions.question: How could a student summarize the whole passage in a faith-centered way?
questions.answer: The order, variety, and purposeful design in animals and birds all point clearly to Allah’s necessary existence and absolute oneness.

questions.question: In this passage, what shared role do animals and birds have?
questions.answer: They serve as collective witnesses to Allah.

questions.question: What is the result of combining the three truths mentioned at the start?
questions.answer: Together they produce one united testimony for divine oneness.

questions.question: How is the scale of this testimony described?
questions.answer: It is described as so vast that the whole earth seems to voice it.

questions.question: What does the traveller’s full understanding tell us about the evidence presented?
questions.answer: It tells us the evidence is strong enough to be recognized with certainty.

questions.question: What kinds of features in animals are described as eloquent and well-ordered?
questions.answer: Their senses, capacities, limbs, organs, and tools within their bodies.

questions.question: Why might bodily parts be described as persuasive?
questions.answer: Because their usefulness and harmony strongly point to wise design.

questions.question: What three actions of Allah toward living things are highlighted in the passage?
questions.answer: Bringing them into being, giving them distinct beauty, and shaping them with proper measure.

questions.question: Why does the passage repeatedly stress order?
questions.answer: Because order is evidence against randomness and in favor of intentional creation.

questions.question: What is the importance of animals being distinct from one another?
questions.answer: Their differences show detailed knowledge and intentional choice in creation.

questions.question: What contrast is made between origins and outcomes?
questions.answer: Similar and limited beginnings lead to an enormous variety of highly organized creatures.

questions.question: Why is that contrast meaningful for belief in Allah?
questions.answer: It shows that the source of variety must be the Creator, not the simple materials themselves.

questions.question: What conclusion about divine power can be drawn from the passage?
questions.answer: Divine power is able to produce endless forms with precision from very small and similar beginnings.

questions.question: What statement of belief stands at the center of the whole passage?
questions.answer: That Allah alone is the one true God.

questions.question: What is the passage trying to prove through the world of animals?
questions.answer: It is trying to prove Allah’s necessary existence and unity.

questions.question: How do the three truths function in the argument?
questions.answer: They work together as supporting lines of evidence for one conclusion.

questions.question: What does the earth-sized image of testimony suggest about the number of witnesses?
questions.answer: It suggests that the witnesses are so many that their message fills the whole world.

questions.question: Which created features are treated like meaningful expressions in this passage?
questions.answer: Animal abilities, senses, limbs, organs, and bodily systems.

questions.question: What do these meaningful expressions say without spoken language?
questions.answer: They point to praise of Allah and to His being the Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage connect creation with intentionality?
questions.answer: It says living beings are brought into existence through will, not by mindless processes.

questions.question: Why is decoration mentioned along with distinction?
questions.answer: Because the beauty and uniqueness of creatures strengthen the evidence of careful design.

questions.question: How does measured shaping support the idea of wisdom?
questions.answer: It shows creatures are formed with balance and suitability rather than disorder.

questions.question: What beginnings of animal life are mentioned in the final part?
questions.answer: Eggs and reproductive drops.

questions.question: Why does the passage emphasize that these beginnings are similar and limited?
questions.answer: To show that the huge range of creatures cannot be explained by those beginnings alone.

questions.question: Which is closer to the passage’s view: animals are accidental products, or animals are signs of divine action? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: Animals are signs of divine action, because their order, variety, and purposeful form all point to Allah.

questions.question: Give a brief main-idea summary of the passage.
questions.answer: The animal world, in all its organized and varied forms, serves as a powerful witness to Allah’s oneness and creative power.

questions.question: What united testimony comes from all species of animals, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They all testify to the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: What literary image is used to describe the earth’s participation in this testimony?
questions.answer: The earth is imagined as a great person making a declaration of faith.

questions.question: Why is this image important for understanding the message?
questions.answer: It shows that the testimony is not small or isolated, but world-encompassing.

questions.question: What does the traveller come to understand from this scene?
questions.answer: He comes to a clear and complete understanding of the truth being shown.

questions.question: In the described formula of testimony, what parts of animals are especially mentioned?
questions.answer: Their senses, faculties, powers, limbs, members, and bodily instruments.

questions.question: What do the order and balance of these parts point to?
questions.answer: They point to a Creator who acts with knowledge and care.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the act of creating living beings?
questions.answer: It presents creation as a deliberate act carried out by divine will.

questions.question: How are purpose and decoration connected in the passage?
questions.answer: The beauty and distinction of creatures are shown as intentional and meaningful, not pointless.

questions.question: What does wisdom have to do with proportion and form here?
questions.answer: Wisdom is seen in giving each creature a fitting structure and measured design.

questions.question: How does the passage use biological beginnings as evidence?
questions.answer: It points out that very similar starting materials become very different creatures in a highly ordered way.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that eggs and reproductive drops are finite?
questions.answer: To stress that limited materials cannot by themselves account for limitless variety.

questions.question: What does “orderly, distinct, variegated” creation suggest about the Creator?
questions.answer: It suggests mastery, knowledge, and purposeful artistry.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is the passage using overall?
questions.answer: It is using signs in creation to reason toward belief in Allah.

questions.question: What is the strongest overall conclusion a student should take from this passage?
questions.answer: The created qualities of animals and birds form a clear, united proof of Allah’s existence, power, wisdom, and oneness.
